questions.prompt: A traffic-lane control light with an illuminated red "X" means:
questions.explanation: A red X over a lane means you must not drive in that lane. A green arrow pointing down means the lane is open.

choices.text: Prepare for an emergency vehicle travelling in that lane
Reduce speed to below 30 km/h
Use that lane only for the purpose of making a left turn
Travel is not permitted in that lane

questions.prompt: A driver approaching a flashing red traffic light must:
questions.explanation: Treat a flashing red light like a stop sign: come to a complete stop, then go only when it is safe. Key words: "flashing red traffic light".

choices.text: Stop and wait for the flashing green light
Reduce speed and proceed with caution
Stop and proceed only when safe to do so
Stop until the signal light turns green

questions.prompt: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light warns of a hazard or a busy intersection. Slow down and proceed with caution. Key words: "flashing yellow".

choices.text: Proceed with caution
The traffic light will turn green
Stop until the light stops flashing
The traffic light will turn red

questions.prompt: Is a driver allowed to turn right at a red traffic control light?
questions.explanation: You may turn right on a red light after coming to a complete stop, unless a sign prohibits it. Yield to pedestrians and traffic first. Key words: "stops", "no traffic, pedestrian or sign".

choices.text: Yes, but only when a sign permits such a turn
Yes, if the driver reduces speed and there is no traffic or pedestrian in the intersection, and no sign that prohibits such a turn
Yes, if the driver stops and there is no traffic, pedestrian or sign that prohibits such a turn
No, right turns on a red traffic light are never permitted

questions.prompt: When approaching an intersection displaying a steady yellow traffic light:
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means the light is about to turn red. Stop before the intersection unless you are so close that you cannot stop safely.

choices.text: Proceed since the light is about to turn green
Yield to vehicles on the right
Stop before the intersection unless the stop cannot be made in safety
Increase speed to clear the intersection

questions.prompt: A solid yellow line together with a broken yellow line marked on the centre of a highway means:
questions.explanation: When a solid and a broken yellow line run side by side, the line closest to you applies. If the broken line is on your side, you may pass when it is safe; if the solid line is on your side, you may not.

choices.text: The road narrows ahead
If the solid line is on your side, passing is permitted
If the broken line is on your side, passing is not permitted
If the broken line is on your side, passing is permitted

questions.prompt: When approaching an intersection and facing a traffic control light that is showing a green right-turn arrow and a red light, a driver:
questions.explanation: Must proceed cautiously in the direction of the arrow (right turn) when it's safe to do so, without stopping, as the arrow specifically permits the turn, overriding the solid red light for that specific movement, but always yield to pedestrians and other traffic.

choices.text: Must stop and wait for a green light before turning in the direction of the arrow
May go straight through the intersection without stopping
May proceed when safe, without stopping, in the direction of the arrow
May turn left without stopping

questions.prompt: A single solid white line between driving lanes in an urban area means:
questions.explanation: In Alberta , a solid white line means you are in a lane of traffic moving in the same direction, and changing lanes across it is generally not permitted or strongly discouraged for safety, especially in urban areas or where it separates lanes of traffic going the same way. A broken white line permits lane changes, while a solid white line means stay in your lane unless it's a designated turn lane.

choices.text: It is an line separating traffic travelling in opposite directions
Traffic on the right is moving faster than traffic on the left
Lane changing is not permitted
Lane changing is permitted

questions.prompt: When facing a solid red light, where must you stop?
questions.explanation: Stop before the stop line or crosswalk in front of you. If there is neither, stop before the intersection. (Driver's Guide p. 22)

choices.text: Inside the crosswalk, so you can see cross traffic
At the edge of the intersection, past the stop line
Before the stop line or crosswalk, or before the intersection if there is neither
Anywhere within 10 metres of the light

questions.prompt: When is a left turn permitted on a red light?
questions.explanation: Unless a sign prohibits it, the only left turn allowed on a red light is from a one-way street onto a one-way street, after a complete stop and yielding to other traffic. (Driver's Guide p. 22)

choices.text: From a one-way street onto a one-way street, after a complete stop
From any street, after a complete stop
Only when there is no oncoming traffic
Never

questions.prompt: A solid double red light has the same meaning as:
questions.explanation: A solid double red light has the same meaning as a single red light. (Driver's Guide p. 22)

choices.text: A flashing red light
A single solid red light
A four-way stop
A red X lane signal

questions.prompt: The light turns yellow while you are already in the intersection. What should you do?
questions.explanation: Drivers already in the intersection when the light turns yellow must safely clear the intersection. (Driver's Guide p. 22)

choices.text: Stop immediately where you are
Reverse back behind the stop line
Wait in the intersection for the next green light
Safely clear the intersection

questions.prompt: What is a "stale" green light?
questions.explanation: A stale green light has been green for a while and will soon turn yellow. Be prepared to stop. (Driver's Guide p. 22)

choices.text: A green light that is flashing
A green light that has burned out
A green light that has just turned green
A green light that has been on for a while and will soon turn yellow

questions.prompt: Approaching a green light, how can you tell it may be about to change?
questions.explanation: Check the pedestrian signal. If it shows "Don't Walk", the light may soon change, so be ready to stop. (Driver's Guide p. 23)

choices.text: The pedestrian signal shows "Walk"
The light is brighter than usual
There is no traffic waiting on the cross street
The pedestrian signal shows "Don't Walk"

questions.prompt: You face a green arrow together with a solid green light. You may:
questions.explanation: With a green arrow and a solid green light, you may proceed in the arrow's direction without yielding. You may go in the other directions when it is safe and legal. (Driver's Guide p. 23)

choices.text: Proceed only in the direction of the arrow
Stop, then proceed when safe
Proceed only after the arrow turns off
Proceed in the direction of the arrow without yielding

questions.prompt: What does a flashing green traffic light mean?
questions.explanation: You may go through, turn left, or turn right without stopping. Opposing traffic faces a red light, but you must still yield to pedestrians and vehicles lawfully in the intersection. (Driver's Guide p. 23)

choices.text: Stop, then proceed when safe
The light is about to turn red
Only pedestrians may proceed
You may go through or turn without stopping, yielding to pedestrians and vehicles in the intersection

questions.prompt: When the traffic lights in all directions are flashing red, the intersection becomes:
questions.explanation: When lights in all directions are flashing red, the intersection becomes a four-way stop. (Driver's Guide p. 23)

choices.text: An uncontrolled intersection
A yield intersection
Closed to all traffic
A four-way stop

questions.prompt: On a vertical traffic signal, in what order are the lights from top to bottom?
questions.explanation: On a vertical signal, red is at the top, yellow in the centre, and green at the bottom. On a horizontal signal, red is on the left. (Driver's Guide p. 22)

choices.text: Green, yellow, red
Yellow, red, green
Red, green, yellow
Red, yellow, green

questions.prompt: A green arrow pointing down over a traffic lane means:
questions.explanation: A downward green arrow over a lane means you may drive in that lane. A red X means you may not. (Driver's Guide p. 24)

choices.text: You may drive in that lane
The lane ends ahead
The lane is for turning only
Move out of that lane

questions.prompt: A pedestrian is halfway across when the signal changes to "Don't Walk". What may the pedestrian do?
questions.explanation: Pedestrians who have already started crossing when "Don't Walk" appears may continue and clear the crosswalk. (Driver's Guide p. 23)

choices.text: Stop and wait in the middle of the road
Continue crossing and clear the crosswalk
Return to the curb they started from
Wait for drivers to wave them on

questions.prompt: What do yellow lane lines tell you?
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic travelling in opposite directions. The yellow line should always be on the driver's left. (Driver's Guide p. 38)

choices.text: Traffic on each side travels in the same direction
The lane is reserved for buses
Traffic on each side travels in opposite directions
Parking is permitted along the line

questions.prompt: What do white lane lines tell you?
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes of traffic travelling in the same direction. (Driver's Guide p. 39)

choices.text: Traffic on each side travels in opposite directions
Traffic on each side travels in the same direction
Passing is never allowed
The road edge is ahead

questions.prompt: A broken white line between two lanes means:
questions.explanation: Broken white lines mean lane changing is permitted, when it is safe. (Driver's Guide p. 39)

choices.text: Lane changing is not permitted
Lane changing is permitted when safe
Traffic in the lanes moves in opposite directions
The lane is ending

questions.prompt: Within an urban area, may you pass across a single solid yellow line?
questions.explanation: Passing safely is permitted across a single solid yellow line within an urban area. In all other cases, single or double solid yellow lines mean no passing. (Driver's Guide p. 38)

choices.text: No, never
Only on one-way streets
Only to pass a cyclist
Yes, if it can be done safely

questions.prompt: Double solid yellow lines on the centre of a road mean:
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean passing is not permitted in either direction. (Driver's Guide p. 38)

choices.text: Passing is not permitted in either direction
Passing is permitted for both directions
Passing is permitted for the right lane only
The road is one-way

questions.prompt: Who may use a two-way left-turn lane in the centre of a road?
questions.explanation: A two-way left-turn lane is shared by left-turning traffic from both directions. You may cross the solid yellow line to enter it, close to where you turn. (Driver's Guide pp. 39, 67)

choices.text: Only traffic turning left from one direction
Any vehicle wanting to pass slower traffic
Emergency vehicles only
Left-turning traffic from both directions

questions.prompt: A white diamond painted on a lane means:
questions.explanation: Diamond markings show that a lane is reserved for specific vehicles, such as buses, taxis, or bicycles. Signs may give the times. (Driver's Guide p. 39)

choices.text: The lane is reserved for specific vehicles
The lane is a passing lane
There is a hazard ahead
The lane is closed

questions.prompt: When may a driver enter a bicycle lane?
questions.explanation: Vehicles may not drive in bicycle lanes, except when turning or entering or leaving a parking spot. Watch carefully for cyclists. (Driver's Guide p. 40)

choices.text: Only when turning or entering or leaving a parking spot
Whenever no cyclists are present
To pass a slow vehicle on the right
During rush hour only

questions.prompt: A painted island (a striped area on the road) means:
questions.explanation: Painted islands are not to be used for travel, and you must not park or stop on them. You may cross one only to enter or leave a driveway, alley, or private drive. (Driver's Guide p. 40)

choices.text: It is a passing lane for slow traffic
It is a waiting area for left turns
Don't travel, stop, or park on it, except to cross into or out of a driveway
It is a parking area for emergency vehicles

questions.prompt: A large white X painted on a rural highway warns of:
questions.explanation: X markings on rural highways show that you are approaching a railway crossing. An advance warning sign will also be posted. (Driver's Guide p. 40)

choices.text: A railway crossing ahead
A closed lane ahead
An intersection with no signs
A school zone ahead

questions.prompt: A bicycle symbol with two chevrons (arrows) above it painted in a traffic lane means:
questions.explanation: This marking guides cyclists and reminds drivers to expect cyclists in the same travel lane. (Driver's Guide p. 40)

choices.text: Bicycles are not allowed in this lane
This lane is for bicycles only
Expect cyclists to share this lane with you
A bicycle crossing is ahead
